I also had run a census search, additional census search as this person wasn't found in the first run of searches and I did eventually find her in the census, but with misspelled name but was able to confirm all the personal details as reported by her husband. So it is not a new victim, it is a victim already included in the schedules.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now please have 65 ter 564 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And Dr. Tabeau, you indicated earlier that you are familiar with this document. Can you tell us as briefly as possible what this document sets out?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It's the so-called census, so-called I'm saying because it was just a survey and the survey was run by the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska in early 1995. In this so-called survey, numbers of the size of ethnic groups in the territory of the Banja Luka sector were produced. I think the date of this document is February 1995, early 1995, as part of the result from this survey, there is the ethnic composition in a number of municipalities in the Banja Luka sector presented as of approximately this moment. In addition to this, this document contains as well for reference purposes some 1991 census figures, also by ethnicity in the same municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In preparation for your testimony in another case recently, did you analyse how the data on population change related to seven of the municipalities contained in this document compared to your data for the same municipalities.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I analysed this information in the Stanisic-Zupljanin case and prepared summary graphs and some summary tables, so there our conclusion was that the pattern and the size -- approximate size of changes in that composition, that we obtained in our project on IDP's and refugees and what is shown in this document are very consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In preparation for your --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sorry, can we please have page 17 in English and page 15 in B/C/S. It's the last page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In preparation for your testimony here today did you compare the figures on the last page of the document which appear to be figures for the entire region with results obtained from your data for the area that eventually ended up in the RS?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. I produced my statistics, based on my sources, that means the population census and the voters' register 1997, 1998, for the same municipalities that are indicated in the MUP document of 1995. It was interesting to see a very high level of similarity of what the 1995 document is showing us compared with the statistics I obtained from my data. There will be small differences of course because the timing is different. I have data as of 1997/8. Here it is 1995, early 1995, also might be some territorial differences as I don't think they analysed, as a matter of fact, the very same territories as I did due to the war activities, but I think generally it is the same territory, slightly different time-period, high similarity of the results.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this document at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objection, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P1656, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could I ask one question, a question for clarification. Page 17 of this document and we see the document now for the first time, isn't it, Mr. Farr, or was it --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you the following: We see in 1991, well, substantial number of Yugoslavs, whereas in 1995, apparently the Yugoslavs is not a category. At the same time the Yugoslavs have not become certainly not all of them -- they are not now under the category of others because the 17.000 at least it's unlikely that all the 52.000 are now part -- or what remains of them are now part of the 17.000. If the Yugoslavs in 1995 have found their way into one of the traditional ethnical groups, to what extent would that create difficulties in interpreting the material? You see my point if someone said, I'm a Yugoslav, in 1991, and if he says in 1995, I'm a Serb, that's ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they might have been included under Serbs in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Difficulties, now, the number of Serbs increased of course by 1995 considerably, if we compare the number of Serbs in 1991 with 1995, it is obvious it is a far higher number. And at the same time the Yugoslavs disappeared, my assumption would be that some of them just moved out and some might have reported themselves as Serbs. I don't think it is, here obviously there is some bias related to the reporting of ethnicity, but generally, I don't think that this bias is considerable and we can still compare the statistics. So the population of non-Serbs was outflowing from these territories at high numbers during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless the Yugoslav were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, with the Yugoslavs, it depends on the context, how they see themselves. In this particular case they would report themselves as Serbs if they wanted to stay in Republika Srpska, I think, but it is not so that I would agree that all of them just changed the self-perception in order to stay because it wasn't easy to live in this territory, so it is as other known Serbs were living, so were the Yugoslavs I believe, because Yugoslavs it's not that simple that all of them were from mixed marriage, Serb plus another ethnicity, so Yugoslav means as well other mixed marriages between Muslim and Croats, for instance, or just people who identify themselves as Yugoslavs, they perceive themselves as Yugoslavs, as a separate ethnic category. In the census there were 98 categories reported, ethnicity was an open-ended question, so anything could be reported and Yugoslavs were reported explicitly as a separate ethnic group, and I have no reason to believe it was not possible for people to feel Yugoslavs. There were people who didn't feel Serb, Croat, any other ethnicity, they felt we were Yugoslavs there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the only reason why I'm raising it because we have an increase of Serbs from 1991 to 1995 of approximately 70.000 more or less in number on a total population which decreased considerably, and just -- I do understand that it may be very unlikely that suddenly all the Yugoslavs became Serbs, but theoretically -- I see your point, that of course there's knowledge about who declared themselves Yugoslavs, but it's difficult perhaps to estimate exactly what proportion of the increase of Serbs and what proportion of the decrease of the total population may be explained by what the Yugoslavs -- or what the persons who declared themselves Yugoslavs in 1991 where they are found in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand exactly what Your Honour is saying but it's impossible to provide a quantitative measure that would answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not saying, I'm just asking myself whether there is a question which is where there's no quantitative answer to that yet, and therefore that it should make us a bit cautious about the percentages, perhaps not but the 10th of per cent but by 1 or 2 and then the matter is how important 1 or 2 per cent would be on the totality of the study. If you'd like to add anything to this, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in my study, there is no ethnic bias, and I have some results related to these particular municipalities which I can share with everybody in this courtroom and from this we see that there is an increase in the Serbs in these territories and this increase is not biased, it's unbiased, it's based on the ethnic definition from 1991 census. That's the answer I can provide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you did not -- comparing this with your study where there's no bias as far as ethnicity is concerned, this, although not entirely easy to interpret, nevertheless gives the same picture as yours, where we know that there's no bias as far as ethnicity is concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, I've stolen another 3 minutes of your time. And I think there were four left.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, could I ask you to -- looking at your two reports together, could you tell us comparing them in a big picture sense what conclusions can be drawn by looking at the reports together, and in other words, does the IDP's and refugees report provide any context to the victims' report and vice-versa in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: First of all, it is important to note that the scale of displacement as we present it in our report is not usual. It is most definitely that there were large numbers of displaced persons, extraordinary large numbers of displaced persons internally and externally. We identified the displacement as of 1997/8, so comparing 1991 with 1997/8 leaves a certain period between which is kind of uncovered by this report. However there must have been some push factors that forced the population to change the place of residence in this period and because of the scale we need to think that these factors operated in the conflict period. So this is one remark about the IDP's refugees report. When we take the victims' report, this report provides some context for the factors, push factors that were operating during the conflict period. It is not so that there were no reasons for the population to leave the houses and move in large numbers to other places. So these factors, unusual factors must be seen as reported in the victims' report, so there is a timing of killings and disappearances reported in the victims' report, there are municipalities assessed from the point of view of the killings and disappearing. So the victims' report most definitely can be seen as the context for the IDP's and refugees report.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I now just have a couple of questions about the proofing note dated 24 November 2010 which has been uploaded as 5867. Did you review a list of discrepancies between the indictment schedules and your proof of death chart and give your comments on what you believe to be the reasons for those differences?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. I did review these differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And are those recorded in the proofing note dated 24 November 2010?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's the note. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And did that proofing note also contain the the list of the names of the 29 victims from this case who you identified as having military status?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, I identified 29 cases reported as militaries, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And finally, does the proofing note also contain --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I see we don't have the right document on the screen. I may have misidentified it; it may be 5866.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And finally, does the proofing note also contain corrections to a number of typographical errors in your report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I have a number of items to tender and to keep it simple, I'll go step by step. First the two reports IDP's and refugees report, which is 65 ter 5864 and the victims' report, which is 5748.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we go step by step. Let's first go to the IDP's and refugees report. Any objections against admission? Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 5864 becomes Exhibit P1657, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. I did not take them together. The victims report, any objections to that? No objections, no reservation as far as the 14 additional --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have -- I apologise if my colleague wanted to speak. I was just about to say that perhaps it should be left as an MFI until we establish what the circumstances are surrounding these 14 victims, that would be my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, do you you agree with that or would you say it's just irrelevant evidence if so, which might be a reason not to be admitted on that portion, but.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, our position would that be all of the evidence concerning victims not referred to on the indictment must be directed to some other purpose than the evidence concerning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Than to prove the killing of those persons in relation to the indictment, that's what your position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the only objection from both Defence teams. I think under those circumstances, we would MFI the document and then decide on admission together with the -- with the decision on the motion to add to the 65 ter list. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 5748 becomes P1658, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And keeps that status. Mr. Farr, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: The next items are the two demonstrative exhibits, that would be 65 ter 5862 for the IDP's and refugees report, and 5863 for the victims report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 5862 becomes P1659 and document 5863 becomes P1660, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1659 and P1660 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: The next item, Your Honour, is the proofing note dated 24 November 2010. That's 65 ter number 5866, if I'm correct this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 5866 becomes P1661, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1661 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau's CV, which is 65 ter 5867 and I would just note that this version is not on our 65 ter list, so this is a motion to add it to our 65 ter list simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection against the CV being added to 65 ter list or to admission? No, then leave is granted to add the CV to the 65 ter list and the Exhibit number Madam Registrar would be?

utterances.text: Document 5867 becomes P1662, Your Honours.

utterances.text: We'll have a look at it, whether we change the status or -- because it also explains some of the circumstance and to that extent, it might even be relevant to our decision that it's not the result of but the explanation of to some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we leave it for the time being and P1662 is admitted into evidence. That's the updated CV.
